subject.title: Docker sandbox exec cancellation doesn't stop the container-side command (orphan keeps running)

question: Should the fix be scoped to Docker sandbox exec cancellation now, or broadened to SSH/remote sandbox process lifecycle in the same change?
rationale: The Docker source path is high-confidence, but the kill strategy affects sandbox isolation, container reuse, and possible cross-command side effects; the SSH sibling is only a hypothesis so automation should not choose that scope alone.

options.title: Fix Docker now
options.body: Implement daemon-side Docker exec teardown with live Docker proof, and open or link a separate SSH follow-up only after reproduction.

options.title: Broaden all remote backends
options.body: Require one design that covers Docker and SSH cancellation together, accepting a larger review and proof burden before implementation.

options.title: Defer for lifecycle design
options.body: Pause this issue behind a broader sandbox process-lifecycle decision if maintainers want one unified remote-exec ownership model first.

recommendation.title: Fix Docker now
recommendation.body: Implement daemon-side Docker exec teardown with live Docker proof, and open or link a separate SSH follow-up only after reproduction.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent blame and sandbox/exec history make steipete the best available owner for the sandbox teardown boundary decision.
